subject: Unit economics follow-up: token volumes & $/1M token targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jason Liu <jason.liu@fintechx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: unit economics & next steps

Hi Jason - great to meet you and the FintechX team today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

- Use case: customer support summarization + automated KYC triage in pilot (Q3).
- Expected peak traffic: 500k calls/month during pilot, scaling to ~5M calls/month in year 1.
- Average prompt length today: ~250 tokens request, 350 tokens response (rough estimate).
- Target unit economics: looking for inference cost ~$/1M tokens in the low hundreds to keep feature-level margin healthy.

Questions we had for you: can you confirm the expected monthly token volumes (request + response) and an internal target $/1M tokens or monthly budget range we should align to? Jason, if you can share the procurement cadence and any target CAC/payback expectations that would help us model pricing.

Next steps:
1) Jason to share a 3-month token volume forecast + budget range (action: FintechX)
2) We to run a unit-econ model and propose pricing/commit bands (action: Marissa + Rishi)
3) Sync with Procurement if numbers match (action: Jason + Procurement)

Attaching a simple volume template - fill the monthly estimates and return and we'll run the $/feature and CAC payback scenarios.

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1-415-555-0198

Attachment: FintechX_MonthlyVolumes.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Jason Liu <jason.liu@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: unit economics & next steps

Thanks Marissa - appreciate the summary. Quick answers below and attached a rough forecast.

- Pilot (Q3): 500k calls/mo estimated -> tokens estimate: 500k * (250+350) = 300M tokens/mo.
- Year 1 target: 5M calls/mo -> ~3B tokens/mo.
- Procurement budget for pilot: ~$18k-$25k/mo. Year 1 target TBD but aim to keep inference spend <10% of gross margin per feature.
- CAC/payback: for this feature we're targeting 3-6 month payback on CAC; early customers average LTV x 3 with payback window target 4 months.

Attaching the filled volume sheet.

Jason
Head of Product, FintechX
jason.liu@fintechx.com

Attachment: FintechX_MonthlyVolumes.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jason Liu <jason.liu@fintechx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: unit economics & next steps

Jason - perfect, that's exactly what we needed. A few quick clarifying Qs so our unit-econ model is aligned:

1) When you say "inference spend <10% of gross margin per feature", do you have a target $/1M tokens in mind we should use for our proposal? If not, we'll present tiered $/1M token bands with commit levels.
2) For the pilot budget ($18k-$25k/mo) - is that committed spend (reserved) or flexible/consumption?
3) Can you share an LTV per customer and avg new customers per quarter assumptions? This helps refine CAC payback math but if you prefer we'll model a range.

We'll run three scenarios: conservative (no commit, pay-as-you-go), mid (quarterly commit with modest discount), and committed (annual or large monthly commit with best unit pricing). I'll include $/feature, CAC payback, and margin sensitivity tables.

If okay, we'll target a follow-up with Rishi (pricing lead) next week to walk through the model.

Best,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: FintechX unit econ - prep for pricing model

Rishi / Monica - FYI thread with FintechX (Jason). Key points:
- Pilot: ~300M tokens/mo, budget $18k-$25k/mo (likely flexible).
- Year1 scale: up to ~3B tokens/mo.
- Target payback: 3-6 months.
- Wants inference spend <10% of gross margin for the feature.

Please help me model the following quickly:
A) $/1M token bands that would hit the pilot budget at 300M tokens (e.g., $X/1M * 300 = $18k-$25k) - show PAYG vs 3mo commit vs 12mo commit.
B) $/feature: assuming the feature drives $Y revenue per account (we can model $50/$100/$200) and given target 10% spend cap, what $/1M token ceiling aligns?
C) CAC payback sensitivity at those $/1M token prices given payback target 3-6 months.

I attached a quick model skeleton - fill in assumptions and recommended bands. Meeting with Jason next Tue, want to show 2 recommended packages.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: FintechX unit econ - prep for pricing model

Thanks Marissa - ran quick numbers and attached the CSV model (RMI_unit_econ_model.csv). High level:

- To hit $18k-$25k at 300M tokens: $/1M token range = $60-$83.3 (PAYG).
- With a 3mo commit (10% discount), bands become ~$54-$75/1M. With a 12mo commit (20% discount), bands become ~$48-$66/1M.
- For $/feature scenarios: if feature generates $100/mo revenue per account, and target inference spend <10% of gross margin, the inference budget per account should be <$10/mo. That maps to token consumption per account limits; at $60/1M -> $10 buys ~166.7k tokens/month (~250 token req/resp = ~667 calls/month).
- CAC payback: at $60/1M and avg revenue per account $100/mo, our models hit ~4 month payback assuming 10% conversion and avg CAC $400. Higher commit discounts push payback to ~3.5 months.

Recommendation (two packages to present):
1) Pilot (Flexible): PAYG at $70/1M with monthly overage; aligns to their stated flexible budget (~$21k at 300M).
2) Committed (Best): 12mo commitment at $55/1M (effective), includes 10% onboarding credit and 60-day SLA window.

I attached the model with sensitivity tabs. Happy to join the call.

-Rishi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jason Liu <jason.liu@fintechx.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: unit economics & next steps

Jason - attaching the model Rishi prepared and a short summary. Two clean options we recommend for FintechX based on your forecast:

1) Flexible Pilot:
- PAYG list: $70 / 1M tokens
- Expected pilot cost @300M tokens: ~$21k/mo (within your $18k-$25k range)
- No minimum commit, 30-day payment terms, standard support

2) Committed Annual (best economics):
- Effective price: $55 / 1M tokens (12mo commit)
- Expected pilot-equivalent cost: ~$16.5k/mo (if you were to apply the effective rate to pilot volumes)
- Includes onboarding credit and priority SLA

High-level CAC & margin notes: at $55-$70/1M our model shows feature-level inference spending stays under 10% for revenue-per-account scenarios >= $90/mo and CAC payback in the target 3-6 month window given typical CAC ranges you shared. We can produce a per-account consumption plan if you want to bound tokens per account.

Proposed next steps:
- Jason: confirm preferred option (Flexible vs Committed) and whether Procurement prefers a commit-based pricing structure (action: FintechX)
- If Committed: we'll send a preliminary commercial term sheet and DocuSign (action: Redwood)
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review the model live (action: all)

Attaching: RMI_unit_econ_model.csv, FintechX_MonthlyVolumes.xlsx

Thanks - happy to hop on a call with Rishi for the pricing walk-through.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: RMI_unit_econ_model.csv (CSV stub), FintechX_MonthlyVolumes.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
